title: A finite tame cover has an etale model after a simultaneous finite root base change
statement:
Let $k$ be a field of characteristic a positive prime $p$, and let $V=\operatorname{Spec}B$ be a regular Noetherian separated scheme of finite type over $k$ [def-weil-regular-scheme, def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions]. Let $t_1,\ldots,t_r\in B$, with $r\geq0$, be such that $V(t_1\cdots t_r)$ is a reduced strict normal crossings boundary [def-trf-strict-normal-crossings-boundary] and at every point $v\in V$ the $t_i$ vanishing at $v$ are part of a regular system of parameters of $\mathcal O_{V,v}$ [def-weil-pbc-regular-system-of-parameters]. The closed subschemes $V(t_i)$ need not be irreducible or connected. Set $f=\prod_i t_i$ and $V^\circ=\operatorname{Spec}B[1/f]$, with $f=1$ when $r=0$. Let $P\to V^\circ$ be a finite etale morphism [def-weil-pbc-finite-etale-category]. Assume that for every geometric point $\bar v$ of $V$, writing $A=\mathcal O_{V,\bar v}^{\mathrm{sh}}$ [def-sc-ring-strict-henselization] and $I(\bar v)=\{i:t_i(\bar v)=0\}$, its pullback to the punctured full root tower
$$\varprojlim_{(m,p)=1}\operatorname{Spec}\bigl(A[z_i:i\in I(\bar v)]/(z_i^m-t_i)_{i\in I(\bar v)}\bigr)[1/\prod_{i\in I(\bar v)}t_i]$$
is a finite disjoint union of copies of that tower. Transitions are the power maps for divisibility, and $m$ ranges over positive integers prime to $p$. Then there are a positive integer $n$ prime to $p$ and a finite etale morphism $Z\to V_n$, where
$$V_n=\operatorname{Spec}\bigl(B[x_1,\ldots,x_r]/(x_i^n-t_i)_i\bigr),$$
together with an isomorphism of $V_n^\circ=V_n\times_V V^\circ$-schemes
$$Z\times_{V_n}V_n^\circ\simeq P\times_{V^\circ}V_n^\circ.$$
No connectedness, Galois action, invertibility of $\deg P$, henselian hypothesis, residual-cover hypothesis, or choice of roots of unity is imposed. The empty cover and $r=0$ are allowed.

source.place: Expose IX Proposition 2.1(i)–(iii) and proof, printed pp.133–134: strict-local parameter-root quotient description and etale-local descent of the finite tame normalization; finite-type-over-a-field specialization. The simultaneous finite root level is the qc consequence of the local description, not a statement about infinite coefficient objects.

proof.text: If $V$ is empty, take $n=1$ and $Z=\varnothing$. If $r=0$, then $V^\circ=V$, and $n=1$, $Z=P$ works without using the tower hypothesis. If $P=\varnothing$, take $n=1$, $Z=\varnothing$. In the remaining argument allow degree zero locally. For every positive $a$ prime to $p$ put $C_a=B[x_1,\ldots,x_r]/(x_i^a-t_i)_i$ and $X_a=\operatorname{Spec}C_a$. Iterating the monic-quotient basis gives the finite free $B$-basis $\prod_i x_i^{e_i}$, $0\le e_i<a$. The same presentation represents roots after any scalar extension: both directions fix coefficients and send each root to its named coordinate. For $a\mid b$ the transition $X_b\to X_a$ is defined by $x_{i,a}\mapsto x_{i,b}^{b/a}$; the relations and composition law follow by exponent multiplication.

source.place: Tag 04GG, monic power bases; the simultaneous presentation in ILO IX Proposition 2.1, printed p.133.

proof.text: We first check regularity of every $C_a$ despite the possibly disconnected labels. At a point $v\in V$, the active $t_i$ are distinct regular parameters, so each is prime in $\mathcal O_{V,v}$ by the regular-local UFD boundary lemma. At every point the same assertion shows that $V(t_i)$ is reduced and locally has at most one irreducible component through the point. There are finitely many boundary components. Delete the components not passing through $v$ and invert the inactive $t_i$; shrink to an affine neighbourhood $W$ of $v$. There each remaining $V(t_i)\cap W$ is precisely one reduced integral boundary component, and these components are pairwise distinct. Indeed two components through $v$ cannot belong to one $(t_i)$, because its localized ideal is prime; two active labels cannot name the same component, because associated parameters would make a generator redundant in the full parameter list, contradicting the dimension bound for a generating set of the maximal ideal. The restricted SNC intersection conditions are unchanged. Apply the existing finite-root regularity theorem to these active labels on $W$. It gives a regular Noetherian algebra after adjoining their $a$th roots.

source.place: IX Proposition 2.1 proof, printed p.133, local parameter-root algebra; Stacks 0AG0 (lemma-regular-local-UFD) and 0BIA (lemma-strict-normal-crossings).

proof.text: Adjoin the roots of the inactive labels successively to the algebra just obtained. If $u$ is a unit in a regular ring $D$, then in $D[T]/(T^a-u)$ the class of $T$ is a unit, with inverse $T^{a-1}/u$. The image of the derivative $aT^{a-1}$ is a unit, since $a$ is prime to $p$. The polynomial ring $D[T]$ is regular, so the hypersurface-derivation criterion makes its quotient regular. Induction over the inactive labels proves that $C_a$ is regular on the inverse image of $W$. These opens cover $X_a$, proving its regularity everywhere; $C_a$ is Noetherian also directly from its finite $B$-basis. Thus $C_a$ is normal. At each stalk of $B$, $f$ is a unit times a product of nonzero parameters in a domain, so multiplication by $f$ is injective on $B$. The monic basis then makes multiplication by $f$ injective on $C_a$ as well. Decompose $X_a$ into its finitely many clopen normal integral components. None is contained in $V(f)$: in that product decomposition injectivity excludes the zero component of $f$. Consequently $X_a^\circ=D(f)$ contains every generic point and is dense in every component.

source.place: Tags 00FN, 00OD; more-algebra.tex Tag 07PF (lemma-quotient-regular); regularity and normal components of the parameter-root algebra.

proof.text: Write $P=\operatorname{Spec}D$ over $B[1/f]$, and $D_a=D\otimes_{B[1/f]}C_a[1/f]$. Finiteness is preserved here by the elementary tensor argument: images of any finite module generating set generate the tensor product. Etaleness is preserved by the etale base-change theorem. Let $E_a$ be the integral closure of $C_a$ in $D_a$. On each normal integral component of $X_a$, apply finite-etale-open integral-closure finiteness to $D(f)$ and this finite etale cover. Its conclusion makes the integral closure a finite module on that component. The finite clopen component decomposition therefore makes $E_a$ a finite $C_a$-module. As $C_a$ is Noetherian, the resulting finite-type algebra $E_a$ is of finite presentation. Put $N_a=\operatorname{Spec}E_a$ with its finite map to $X_a$. No Galois closure or degree bound has been introduced.

source.place: Tag 032L (lemma-Noetherian-normal-domain-finite-separable-extension), applied componentwise as in the cited finiteness node; 00FP; morphisms.tex 02GO.

proof.text: The open restriction of $N_a$ is the prescribed cover: apply integral-closure ind-etale base change to $C_a\to C_a[1/f]$. This localization is ind-etale since it is an open immersion and is etale. It identifies $E_a[1/f]$ with the integral closure of $C_a[1/f]$ in $D_a$. Every element of the finite $C_a[1/f]$-algebra $D_a$ is integral, so this closure is all of $D_a$. Also the integral closure of $C_a$ in $C_a[1/f]$ is exactly $C_a$: an integral section on the dense open $D(f)$ extends by the normal dense-open integral-section theorem, and the injection $C_a\hookrightarrow C_a[1/f]$ from Step 3 makes the extension unique. Both assertions use the actual structural maps, not merely abstract isomorphisms.

source.place: Tag 0CBF (lemma-integral-closure-commutes-colim-smooth), with localization; normal integral-section extension, Tag 0AB1.

proof.text: Fix a geometric point $\bar v$ with image $v$ and put $A=\mathcal O_{V,\bar v}^{\rm sh}$ and $I=\{i:t_i(v)=0\}$. The geometric strict-henselization presentation identifies $A$ with the algebraic strict henselization of $B_v$. It is Noetherian and is a filtered colimit of etale $B$-algebras. For $(m,p)=1$, put $T_m=A[z_i:i\in I]/(z_i^m-t_i)_{i\in I}$. The active puncture $T_m[1/\prod_{i\in I}t_i]$ equals $T_m[1/f]$, since all inactive $t_j$ are units in $A$. These affine punctures form a directed inverse system under divisibility with affine transitions. The limit is the tower in the hypothesis, by the affine-transition limit theorem. Each $T_m$ and $T_m[1/f]$ is Noetherian, by the monic finite basis and Noetherian finite-type permanence. The pullbacks of $P$ are etale and of finite presentation: etaleness is base change, and finite module generators give finite-type algebras over these Noetherian bases.

source.place: Tag 01YW, affine inverse limits; more-algebra.tex 06LJ; algebra.tex 04GW; etale-cohomology.tex 04HX.

proof.text: By the hypothesis, over that punctured limit there is an isomorphism from the pullback of $P$ to $d$ copies of the base for some finite $d\ge0$. Apply the morphism and equality clauses of finite-data descent to this isomorphism and its inverse between the pullbacks of $P_A$ and the fixed trivial $d$-sheeted cover, both defined at $m=1$. Descend the two arrows and the two inverse identities, and enlarge to a common prime-to-$p$ index $m$. This gives an isomorphism over $T_m[1/f]$ between $P_A$ pulled back there and $\coprod_d\operatorname{Spec}T_m[1/f]$. All objects at the starting stage are etale of finite presentation, as checked in Step 6; the index is the directed set of positive prime-to-$p$ integers with divisibility. Thus the cited morphism and equality clauses apply to the specified objects, rather than descending an unrelated model of them.

source.place: Tag 01ZM, morphisms and eventual equality, applied to an isomorphism and its inverse on the punctured finite-root system.

proof.text: Let $S=A\otimes_B C_m=A[x_1,\ldots,x_r]/(x_i^m-t_i)_i$. There is a $T_m$-algebra structure on $S$ sending $z_i$ to $x_i$ for active $i$. Base change of the preceding splitting gives the actual $S[1/f]$-algebra isomorphism $D_m\otimes_{C_m}S\simeq S[1/f]^d$. The map $C_m\to S$ is ind-etale: it is the base change of the filtered etale presentation $B\to A$, by ind-etale stability. This argument merely adjoins the roots of the inactive units as additional coordinates; it neither chooses those roots in $A$ nor assumes any roots of unity in $B$.

source.place: Tag 04GW for the strict-local presentation and base change of that presentation; the displayed full root algebra in ILO IX Proposition 2.1.

proof.text: Apply integral-closure ind-etale base change twice along $C_m\to S$. For the algebra $C_m[1/f]$, Step 5 says its integral closure is $C_m$, so the theorem identifies the integral closure of $S$ in $S[1/f]$ with $S$, via the structural inclusion. For the algebra $D_m$, it identifies $S\otimes_{C_m}E_m$ with the integral closure of $S$ in $S[1/f]^d$, using Step 8. This last closure is $S^d$: projection shows that an integral tuple has every coordinate integral, hence in $S$ by the first application; conversely every tuple of elements of $S$ is integral over diagonal $S$, since for $s=(s_1,\ldots,s_d)$ the monic polynomial $\prod_{j=1}^d(T-s_j)$ vanishes coordinatewise. For $d=0$ the target ring is the zero ring and both closures are zero. Hence $N_m\times_V\operatorname{Spec}A$ is a disjoint union of $d$ copies of $X_m\times_V\operatorname{Spec}A$. It is therefore finite etale over that base.

source.place: Tag 0CBF; two explicit applications of integral-closure base change, followed by the coordinatewise monic-polynomial calculation.

proof.text: The map $B_v\to A$ is faithfully flat by strict-henselization faithful flatness; its spectrum is surjective by faithful-flat surjectivity and flat, hence is an fpqc cover (an affine surjective flat map meets the defining affine-cover condition). Fpqc base-change stability makes $\operatorname{Spec}(A\otimes_B C_m)\to\operatorname{Spec}(B_v\otimes_B C_m)$ an fpqc cover. Etaleness thus descends by fpqc descent from Step 9: $N_m\times_V\operatorname{Spec}B_v\to X_m\times_V\operatorname{Spec}B_v$ is etale. Now write $B_v$ as the directed colimit of $B[1/h]$ for $h\notin v$ (the index can be finite subsets of $B\setminus v$, inverting their product). Apply etale-property descent to the fixed finitely presented morphism $N_m\to X_m$ over $V$. All schemes at the starting stage are affine, hence qcqs; the transitions are affine localizations. There is $h_v\notin v$ such that $N_m\to X_m$ is etale after base change from $V$ to $W_v=D(h_v)$. It is still finite there, because a finite module generating set remains generating after localization. Thus a finite root level $m_v=m$ works on an entire Zariski neighbourhood of $v$, including every point of $X_m$ above it.

source.place: Tag 07RP (lemma-descend-etale) for the localization system; descent.tex 02VN; more-algebra.tex 07QM (lemma-dumb-properties-henselization).

proof.text: The opens $W_v$ cover the quasi-compact affine $V$. Choose a finite subcover $W_1,\ldots,W_s$, with corresponding levels $m_1,\ldots,m_s$. Set $n=\prod_{j=1}^s m_j$, a positive integer prime to $p$. For every $j$ the power substitutions from Step 1 give $X_n\to X_{m_j}$. Pull the finite etale cover $N_{m_j}|_{X_{m_j}\times_VW_j}$ back along this map, obtaining $Z_j\to X_n\times_VW_j$. Etaleness is stable under base change, and tensoring module generators proves finiteness. Its restriction to $X_n^\circ\times_VW_j$ is identified with the pullback of $P$ by Step 5. These identifications use the same power substitution for every root and therefore give actual identifications with one fixed cover $P\times_{V^\circ}X_n^\circ$.

source.place: IX Proposition 2.1 proof, printed pp.133-134, locality on the base; explicit quasi-compact finite-level passage.

proof.text: For completeness construct the overlap identifications rather than assuming normalization commutes with the ramified transition $X_n\to X_{m_j}$. The base $X_n$ is normal Noetherian by Steps 2-3. On an overlap $H_{ij}=X_n\times_V(W_i\cap W_j)$, its clopen integral components are normal, and $H_{ij}\cap X_n^\circ$ is dense in each nonempty component, by Step 3 and restriction. The two covers $Z_i,Z_j$ have a specified isomorphism on that dense open through their identifications with the same pullback of $P$. On each integral component restrict this isomorphism to its generic point and apply generic-point full faithfulness for finite etale covers to extend that morphism and its inverse. Their composites are identities by uniqueness at the generic point. These extensions agree with the original isomorphism on the entire punctured overlap: apply uniqueness again on the integral dense open, which is normal. Combining the clopen components gives an isomorphism $\alpha_{ij}:Z_i|_{H_{ij}}\simeq Z_j|_{H_{ij}}$ extending exactly the specified puncture identification.

source.place: IX Proposition 2.1 proof, printed pp.133-134, graph/full-faithfulness argument; algebraic generic-point extension supplied by the cited existing node.

proof.text: On each integral component of a triple overlap, the two composites $\alpha_{jk}\alpha_{ij}$ and $\alpha_{ik}$ agree at the generic point, since all puncture identifications factor through the single cover pulled back from $P$. Uniqueness in generic-point full faithfulness makes them equal everywhere. The same uniqueness gives the identity and inverse conditions. Hence $(Z_j,\alpha_{ij})$ is a finite etale descent datum for the surjective etale morphism $\coprod_j(X_n\times_VW_j)\to X_n$ (each summand is an open immersion). Effective finite-etale descent supplies a finite etale $Z\to X_n$ and compatible identifications with the $Z_j$. Restricting to the puncture, their specified identifications with $P\times_{V^\circ}X_n^\circ$ satisfy the same datum. Full faithfulness of the descent equivalence therefore gives the required isomorphism $Z\times_{X_n}X_n^\circ\simeq P\times_{V^\circ}X_n^\circ$. Since $X_n=V_n$ by its presentation, this is the assertion.
